sources.title: States sue SpaceX to stop Grok from generating child sex images, revenge porn

stories.headline: Virginia and Oregon sue SpaceX over Grok sexual deepfakes
stories.dek: The attorneys general allege Grok generated child abuse imagery and non-consensual nudes while SpaceX and xAI publicly promised the tool was safe.
stories.body:
Virginia Attorney General Jay Jones and Oregon Attorney General Dan Rayfield have sued SpaceX, alleging its Grok AI generated child sexual abuse material (CSAM) and non-consensual intimate images, and that the company misled users about safety. The two states filed separate but similar suits, according to a Virginia release dated November 23. Virginia filed in the Circuit Court for the City of Richmond. Oregon filed in Multnomah County Circuit Court.

The defendant is SpaceX, which the release describes as the operator of the social network X and of xAI, now called "SpaceX Super Intelligence," the developer of the Grok models. Virginia alleges the company failed to stop Grok from producing sexualized images of real people, including children, without their consent. It also alleges SpaceX promoted the platform and the tool as safe at the same time.

The complaint says Grok could turn a single existing photo into a realistic image or video of a person nude, partially nude or engaged in sexual activity. Virginia alleges the company ignored industry-standard safeguards to stand out in the AI race. It also says Grok was marketed as an AI companion with a "rebellious streak" and offered a "spicy mode" that allowed nude and sexualized images. "The lack of needed safety measures was considered a feature, not a bug," Rayfield said.

The filing cites a Center for Countering Digital Harm study. It estimated that between December 29, 2025, and January 8, 2026, Grok created and posted about three million sexualized images on X. About 23,000 of them appeared to depict children. That works out to roughly 190 sexualized images a minute, the release says. Nearly 30 percent of the child images CCDH identified were still public on X a week or more later. Some "removed" images could still be reached through separate URLs, the release says.

"Companies that deploy powerful tools don't get to ignore consumer safety and call it innovation," Jones said. He framed the case around the "millions of Virginians" with X accounts who he says were misled by the company's reassurances.

The release does not include a response from SpaceX, X or xAI. The allegations have not been tested in court, and the specific remedies are not spelled out beyond "significant new protections for consumers."
key_points: Virginia and Oregon filed separate but similar suits against SpaceX
States allege Grok made CSAM and non-consensual intimate images
CCDH estimated 3 million sexualized Grok images in about 11 days
Suits allege a "spicy mode" and false safety claims
stories.why_it_matters: State consumer-protection suits like these test whether AI image generators can be held liable for their outputs and their safety marketing. The outcome could shape the guardrails expected of any company shipping image or video generation.

sources.name: The Neuron (reporting Anthropic engineering report)
sources.title: Anthropic used Claude agents to rewrite its Messages API from Python to Rust

stories.headline: Claude agents help Anthropic rewrite its Messages API in Rust
stories.dek: Anthropic says the port from Python cut per-request CPU use about 70 percent, though verifying Claude's code took months.
stories.body:
Anthropic says Claude agents helped rebuild its Messages API in Rust, replacing the Python version. In a November 25 engineering report, the company said per-request CPU use fell about 70 percent and memory use dropped more than 80 percent, The Neuron reports.

The rewrite also sped up Claude Code. Median time to first token for the coding tool fell 20 percent, according to the report.

The speed of the drafting came with a catch. Claude wrote the core request path in about a week, Anthropic says, but verifying that code took months. That gap is a useful data point for developers weighing AI-assisted rewrites: generating the code was the quick part, and confirming it behaved correctly took far longer.
key_points: Anthropic says Claude agents helped port its Messages API from Python to Rust, per a November 25 engineering report.
Per-request CPU use fell about 70 percent and memory use more than 80 percent; Claude Code's median time to first token dropped 20 percent.
Claude drafted the core request path in about a week, but verification took months.

sources.name: Hacker News
sources.title: Google's DeepCrossAttention achieves comparable model quality up to 3x faster

stories.headline: Google's DeepCrossAttention trains transformers up to 3x faster
stories.dek: A rework of residual connections lets each layer pick which earlier layers to draw from, adding under 0.2 percent more parameters.
stories.body:
Google Research says DeepCrossAttention (DCA), a change to how transformers pass information between layers, reaches the same model quality up to three times faster with a negligible increase in parameters. The work, first presented at ICML 2025, was described in a Google Research blog post on November 23.

Standard residual connections simply add a layer's output to its input, which Google says dilutes details from earlier layers in deep networks. DCA instead uses learnable weights and depth-wise cross-attention to choose which previous layers matter, per token. On the C4 and LM1B datasets, DCA matched standard transformers in up to five times fewer training steps, according to Google. A 30-layer DCA model beat a 42-layer standard model on LM1B perplexity.

Google says similar dynamic residual techniques are spreading, citing Moonshot AI's attention residuals and Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 model.
key_points: DCA adds less than 0.2 percent to model size and can be retrofitted onto pre-trained transformers, Google says.
On LM1B, a 30-layer DCA model outperformed a 42-layer standard transformer, a 29 percent cut in depth.
Retrofitting DCA and continuing training cut LM1B perplexity by 0.19, versus 0.02 for standard continued training.

sources.name: Tom's Hardware
sources.title: AMD and Winbond vulnerabilities let attackers brute-force BitLocker PINs on millions of PCs

stories.headline: AMD and Winbond flaws cut BitLocker PIN cracking to about 20 days
stories.dek: TU Berlin researchers show how cheap hardware can trick the failed-attempt counter on fTPM machines, and no vendor has committed to a root-cause fix.
stories.body:
Researchers at Technische Universität Berlin have found flaws in AMD firmware and Winbond SPI flash that let attackers with physical access brute-force BitLocker PINs, Tom's Hardware reports. Cracking a six-digit numeric PIN drops from 19 years to about 20 days, and possibly hours in some cases.

The attacks defeat the counter that forces a 10-minute wait after 32 failed attempts. On Winbond's RPMC chips, a voltage glitch leaks an HMAC key, letting a cheap interposer fake counter increases. Winbond holds roughly 25 percent of the SPI flash market, according to the paper. AMD's storage controller never verifies that the counter actually increased, so attackers can simply block the command. The team confirmed issues from Zen 2 up to an AI 5 330 laptop.

The Winbond flaw requires replacing the chip. AMD's could be patched via AGESA, but that depends on OEM BIOS updates.
key_points: A six-digit BitLocker PIN that normally takes 19 years to brute-force can fall in about 20 days, Tom's Hardware reports.
Winbond RPMC flash and AMD fTPM systems from Zen 2 onward are affected; attacks require physical access.
No vendor has committed to fixing the root causes; Microsoft now recommends six-digit PINs instead of four.

sources.title: Switzerland Confirms AI-Assisted Cyberattacks Breached Critical Infrastructure Operators

stories.headline: Swiss agency confirms first AI agent cyberattacks on local firms
stories.dek: Attackers using autonomous AI agents broke in at four of five confirmed cases, including two critical infrastructure operators, with no major disruptions reported.
stories.body:
Attackers using AI agents broke into systems at Swiss organizations in four of five confirmed attacks, the country's first such cases, according to Switzerland's National Cyber Security Centre. Director Florian Schütz gave the figures to public broadcaster SRF. Three attacks targeted critical infrastructure operators, and two succeeded, with no major disruptions reported. The victims and the attackers have not been identified.

The agency's Tuesday advisory had said the agents compromised systems in every case known at the time. It has not explained why the count changed. The agency says the number of AI attack tools freely reachable online has nearly doubled since October.

Italy's CSIRT and Britain's NCSC report similar agent-driven campaigns exploiting old weaknesses at speed. Switzerland advises patching critical flaws on internet-facing systems within 24 hours.
key_points: Four of five confirmed AI-agent attacks in Switzerland succeeded, including two of three on critical infrastructure operators.
The Swiss agency says freely reachable AI attack tools have nearly doubled since October.
Italy and the UK report similar campaigns; Switzerland urges patching critical internet-facing flaws within 24 hours.

featured.headline: Divinity: Original Sin 2 drops to its lowest price ever: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Divinity: Original Sin 2 - Definitive Edition is a turn-based tactical RPG with an Overwhelmingly Positive Steam rating and a Metascore of 95, the highest score on today's list. Steam sells it for €11.24, down 75 percent from its regular €44.99. That is the lowest price ever recorded.

The deal ends November 30 at 19:00 CET. It suits players who like story-rich fantasy RPGs and turn-based strategy. A record-low price on a game rated this highly rarely lines up, and the combination of a deep cut, top-tier reviews and a firm end date earns it a Strong Buy.

featured.headline: Hades hits a record low of €6.12 on Steam: Strong Buy
featured.body:
Hades, an action roguelike with hack-and-slash combat and a mythology theme, carries an Overwhelmingly Positive Steam rating and a Metascore of 93. Steam has it at €6.12, a 75 percent cut from the regular €24.50, and the lowest price ever recorded.

The sale runs until December 1 at 19:00 CET. It suits roguelike fans first, but its ratings make it a safe pick for anyone who enjoys fast action games. At this price, with no sign it has ever been cheaper, the deal rates a Strong Buy and stands as the best value among today's indie picks.
